Container.Name: Sanguity
Container.Overview: Your medical records, insurance claims and wearable data on one private timeline, on your own server. Sanguity turns the exports you download from patient portals and insurers, plus watch and smart-scale data from your phone, into one place to see lab trends, visits, hospital stays, documents and what your care cost. Several people, each with their own account and profiles; records are encrypted at rest.[br][br]After the first start, open the Web UI and enter the one-time setup code from the container's log to create the first account. Keep a copy of the Encryption key folder somewhere other than the data and its backups: without it, the records can't be read.

Config.Name: Watch receiver port
Config.Description: Where the phone app (Health Connect webhook) uploads watch and smart-scale data.

Config.Name: Watch receiver port, for the upload address
Config.Description: The Watch receiver port above, again: Sanguity can't see the port Unraid publishes, and gives this one in the phone app's upload address. Change both together.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The database and each profile's files.

Config.Name: Encryption key
Config.Description: The encryption key and the watch receiver's secret, kept apart from the data and its backups. Keep a copy somewhere safe (not with the backups): without it the records can't be read.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where Sanguity writes its backups, on the schedule set under Admin > Backups or with python -m server.manage backup. Copy them off this server too.

Config.Name: Watch data
Config.Description: Watch and smart-scale data from the phone app.

Config.Name: Record exports
Config.Description: Optional: record exports described in sources.json (read-only). Records can also be uploaded in the app.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: Used to assign watch readings to days, e.g. America/Chicago or Europe/London.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the app runs as and owns its files (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the app runs as (100 = users).

Config.Name: Public origins
Config.Description: Only if sign-in says "Request refused (cross-site check)" behind your own reverse proxy: the address you open Sanguity at, e.g. https://health.example.com. Passkeys need an HTTPS address.

Config.Name: Secure cookie
Config.Description: Mark the session cookie Secure: 1 (always) or 0 (never). Empty: auto, Secure when your reverse proxy says the request came over HTTPS. Set here, it can't be changed in the app.
